Description: This dataset shows global land cover at 10-metre resolution, classifying the entire planet's surface into categories like cropland, forest, grassland, built-up area, and water. Detailed enough to pick out individual fields and small water bodies — useful as a base layer for land-use, deforestation, or habitat analysis.

This dataset shows where forest has been lost worldwide each year since 2000, detected from satellite imagery. Useful for tracking deforestation hotspots and trends, tied to agriculture, logging, or fire, with new data added annually.
Source: University of Maryland (Hansen/UMD), with Google, USGS, NASA — distributed via WRI's Global Forest Watch

Description: This dataset was produced for nominal 2010 by overlaying the five dominant crops of the world over the remote sensing derived global irrigated and rainfed cropland area map of the International Water Management Institute to create eight classes of crop dominance.

Dataset Name: Global Human Settlement Layer (GHSL) data layers
Description: This dataset shows where people live and how built-up areas have grown worldwide from 1975 to today, combining satellite imagery with census data. Useful for tracking urban growth, estimating population exposure to disasters, and classifying urban vs. rural areas using a standard UN-recommended method.
Source: European Commission Joint Research Centre (EC JRC)

Description: This dataset shows the intensity of nighttime lights worldwide, captured monthly by satellite. Since light output correlates with human activity, it's commonly used as an indirect proxy for economic activity, electrification, and urbanization — especially where official economic data is sparse or delayed.
Source: NOAA/NCEI Earth Observation Group (hosted by Esri)

Description: Shows the global density of cattle, buffalo, sheep, goats, pigs, and chickens. Useful for food security, livelihoods, health, and environmental analysis
Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

Description: Shows global precipitation estimates using observations from multiple satellites. Useful for tracking precipitation trends, extreme events, and the water cycle.
Timeframe: 1998–present; updated every 30 minutes for near-real-time products

Description: Shows active fires and thermal anomalies detected by satellites around the world. Useful for near-real-time fire monitoring and analysis.
Shows the global extent and change of mangrove forests. Useful for monitoring mangrove conservation and restoration.

GBIF is an open-data infrastructure that makes biodiversity data freely available online; its database contains hundreds of millions to billions of species-occurrence records. Researchers use GBIF for species-distribution modeling, conservation planning, invasive-species research, ecological studies, and analyzing changes in biodiversity over time.

Dataset Name: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Redlist of Threatened Species
Description: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species is the world's most comprehensive information source on the global conservation status and extinction risk of animal, plant and fungal species. It is managed by the IUCN and provides scientific assessments that support conservation planning, policy and biodiversity decision-making.
Source: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
More Information: IUCN Green List of Protected and Conserved Areas

Description: Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS) is a global, open-access database providing information on the distribution and occurrence of marine species and biodiversity. It is particularly relevant for your Blue Biodiversity Knowledge Explorer.

FAOSTAT is a global statistical database, providing free access to food and agriculture statistics for more than 245 countries and territories. It covers areas such as crop and livestock production, food security and nutrition, trade, prices, forestry, fisheries, land use, and agricultural resources.
Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
Format: Data can be explored online or downloaded in formats such as CSV, JSON, XML, and SQL, depending on the dataset.  Mostly tabular / statistical data.
More Information: Food and Agriculture Data, FAO website

Description: A comprehensive global database on fish species providing information on taxonomy, distribution, morphology, habitat, ecology, life history, reproduction, diet, population dynamics, fisheries, conservation, and species-related references.
A comprehensive database of the world’s bird species and subspecies, integrating taxonomic information, regional checklists, synonyms, common names, and distribution information.

AntWeb is a global biodiversity database specifically to ants (Formicidae), it provides specimen records, taxonomic information, high-resolution images, geographic information, and natural-history data.
Source: California Academy of Sciences and GBIF

Description: LandScan displays the average number of people in each 1 km square across the world.
CHIRPS displays daily rainfall every  five days across most of the world since 1981, from 60 degrees south to 60 degrees north.

FishStat is FAO's global fisheries and aquaculture statistical database, providing annual, country- and species-level data on capture fisheries, aquaculture production and related fisheries statistics.
Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

Description: Global Dam Watch maps dams, reservoirs and other structures that block rivers around the world.
An interactive computational tool that offers users quick access to the World Bank’s estimates of poverty, inequality, and shared prosperity
Timeframe: Survey years vary by country; estimates updated periodically

Description: Provides data on HIV epidemiology, programme coverage, and financing.
Source: UNAIDS, with national authorities and partners

Description: Shows land-surface elevation measured by the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission.
an online platform that measures riverine and coastal flood risks under both current baseline conditions and future projections in 2030, 2050, an 2080

Dataset Name: GIRI (Global Infrastructure Risk Model and Resilience Index) Data Platform
Description: Provides global maps and data for exploring disaster risks and infrastructure resilience.
Timeframe: Existing climate conditions; future climate scenarios for 2100

Description: SMAP measures how much moisture is in the top layer of soil across the world every few days.
WaPOR measures water usage by crops and other plants.
Measures water levels in large lakes and reservoirs
GEMStat collects water quality parameters from rivers, lakes and groundwater.
Global gridded climate data providing temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, wind speed, water vapor pressure, and bioclimatic variables.
Provides a global climate and water balance at a monthly scale.
Maps global climate zones, based on temperature and rainfall, that align with similar vegetation.
Maps the path and strength of every recorded tropical storm, typhoon and hurricane globally.
A drought index that measures moisture deficits by calculating precipitation minus potential evapotranspiration.
The aridity index measures how dry a climate is by comparing rainfall with how much water could evaporate.
Monitors drought conditions worldwide using rainfall, soil moisture and vegetation health indicies.
A global catologue of earthquakes that is standardized via magnitude.
Monitors active fires using remote sensing data
Displays how much sunshine and solar generation a site can produce.
Displays how strong and steady the wind is at each place, and estimates how much electricity electricity production.
ThinkHazard! estimates the likelihood of a  natural hazard at a given place from very low to high, and provides guidance on reducing those impact.
The Checklist of CITES Species provides the official list of CITES-listed species and their associated scientific synonyms
AlgaeBase is a global algal database of taxonomic, nomenclatural and distributional information.
Global database of plant functional traits such as plant height, leaf area, seed mass, specific leaf area, wood density, phenology and physiological traits
Source: Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry, Jena, Germany

Description: A global archive compiling regional plant checklists and floras, providing information on the floristic status and distribution of plant species across geographic regions. It also provides plant functional trait information.
A global marine biodiversity database providing taxonomic, biological, ecological, distribution, habitat, life-history, and fisheries-related information for marine species.
Source: Quantitative Aquatics, Inc, and the Sea Around Us at the University of British Columbia.

Description: GenAge is a curated database of genes associated with ageing and longevity in humans and model organisms. It provides information on genes, species, gene functions, and experimental or literature evidence linking specific genes to ageing and lifespan.
Source: Human Ageing Genomic Resources (HAGR), Integrative Genomics of Ageing Group

Description: POWO is a global, Kew-maintained plant biodiversity information database providing taxonomic names, synonyms, descriptions, geographic distributions, images, traits, uses and other information on the world's vascular plants.

Dataset Name: Global Fishing Watch - Ocean monitoring and analysis
Description: Global Fishing Watch (GFW) provides open-access geospatial datasets and data services related to global fishing activity and ocean use. It is a data platform containing multiple datasets.
More Information: Mapping human activity at sea from space

Description: AquaMaps is a global marine biodiversity database and species-distribution mapping system. It provides standardised distribution maps for over 33,500 species of fishes, marine mammals and invertebrates.

FishBase is a global, open-access information system on fish species, containing taxonomic, biological, ecological, distribution, fisheries and conservation-related information, it covers >33,000 fish species.
More Information: Catalogue of Life-Find species and other Taxa by name.

Description: inaturalist help to identify species using the database of wild species available both locally and worldwide.
eBird is an online database of bird observations providing scientists, researchers and amateur naturalists with real-time  data about bird distribution and abundance.
Source: Cornell Lab of Ornithology at Cornell University.

Description: A global catalogue of the world's known species, providing scientific names, accepted names, synonyms, taxonomic classification and species information. It is primarily a taxonomic/nomenclatural database.

ITIS is a taxonomic database, provides standardized scientific names and taxonomic information for organisms. It includes taxonomic hierarchy, synonyms, authorship, common names, and Taxonomic Serial Numbers (TSNs), which provide unique identifiers for taxa.
Source: USGS, Science for Changing World and Smithsonian Institution

Description: Wikispecies is a free, multilingual online taxonomic database that provides information on the classification and scientific names of living organisms.
Index Fungorum provides nomenclatural data for the scientific names of fungi (including yeasts, lichens, chromistan fungal analogues, protozoan fungal analogues and fossil forms) at all ranks.

BIEN is an integrated biodiversity informatics database that combines plant occurrence records, vegetation-plot and survey data, functional trait data, taxonomic information, and species geographic-range data. It integrates records from herbaria, ecological surveys, citizen-science platforms and other botanical datasets.
Source: BIEN is an integrated biodiversity informatics database/ecosystem that combines plant occurrence records, vegetation-plot and survey data, functional trait data, taxonomic information, and species geographic-range data. It integrates records from herbaria, ecological surveys, citizen-science platforms and other botanical datasets

Description: The Checklist of CITES Species provides the official list of CITES-listed species and their associated scientific synonyms

The Mammal Diversity Database (MDD) is a global, continuously updated database of living and recently extinct mammal species and higher taxonomic groups. It tracks taxonomic changes based on current scientific literature and provides information such as accepted names, synonyms, taxonomy, common names, type localities, and geographic distributions.
Source: American Society of Mammalogists (ASM), through its Biodiversity Committee
More Information: Track the latest taxonomic changes to living and recently extinct

Description: Maps at the global cropland at 30 meter resolution.
Maps cropland change from 2000 to 2019 in four year periods.
Maps carbon monoxide in the air, in near real time from  the burning of fuels and biomass.
Provides near real time maps of methane in the air, from wetlands, agriculture,  waste and oil and gas production.
A comprehensive database of the world’s bird species and subspecies, integrating taxonomic information, regional checklists, synonyms, common names, and distribution information.
Global taxonomic database of living reptiles containing species classification, scientific names, synonyms, distribution, type information and literature references.
Source: Maintained by Dr. Peter Uetz and Jirí Hošek, supported by photo editors, taxonomic editors, a Scientific Advisory Board, and numerous volunteers worldwide

Description: A comprehensive global taxonomic database of spiders (Araneae), provides information on currently recognized spider species, genera, families, synonyms, taxonomic classifications, authorship, geographic distribution.

WoRMS is a global taxonomic database, it provides authoritative information on marine species names, synonyms, classification, taxonomic status, and references, covering a wide range of marine organisms.

Dataset Name: International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses (ICTV)
Description: ICTV is the international authority responsible for developing and maintaining the universal classification and nomenclature of viruses. It provides an authoritative taxonomy of viruses, including virus names, taxonomic ranks, and classification information.
Source: International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses (ICTV)

Description: A global biodiversity database and informatics platform that stores DNA barcode sequences linked to specimen, taxonomic, geographic, and collection information. It is primarily used for species identification, DNA barcoding, biodiversity research, and monitoring.
Source: Centre for Biodiversity Genomics (CBG) at the University of Guelph, Canada.
Format: Tabular/TSV data for specimen and metadata records

Description: The Paleobiology Database (PBDB) is a global database of fossil occurrence, taxonomic, geological, and paleobiological information. It contains geographically and geologically referenced records of organisms from different geological ages and is widely used for studying biodiversity through geological time.
Source: The Paleontological Society and University of Wisconsin–Madison

Description: It contains water-quality monitoring data from rivers, lakes, reservoirs, wetlands and groundwater, including physical, chemical and biological parameters.
Provides near-real-time maps of atmospheric formaldehyde, created when volatile organic compounds from plants, fires, traffic, and industry break down in sunlight
The satellite maps total atmospheric ozone, including the high-altitude layer formed by sunlight and ground-level concentrations caused by pollution.
Provide near real time  nitrogen dixoide in the air from shipping, traffic, powerplants and industry.

More Info Link: Provides near real time maps of sulphur dioxide in the air from power plants, smelters and volcanoes.

Description: Shows what covers the land surface worldwide (forest, cropland, grassland, wetland, urban, and more) for every year since 1992. Because the maps are consistent over three decades, this layer is often used to track long-term land cover change and feed climate models.
Source: ESA Climate Change Initiative / Copernicus Climate Change Service

Description: Shows where fires have burned across the world and how much land burned each year, broken down by land cover type. This layer is often used to track wildfire trends, assess damage, and link fire activity to drought and land use.

Shows fires detected by satellites as they happen, anywhere on Earth, with an archive going back two decades. This layer is often used for early warning, monitoring agricultural burning, and spotting fires linked to deforestation.

Shows observed and projected changes in temperature, rainfall, and extremes for regions worldwide, using the data behind the latest IPCC assessment. This layer is often used as the authoritative reference for regional climate change.

Shows past and future values for climate variables and indices such as hot days, heavy rainfall, and drought conditions. This layer is often used to compare how climate hazards may change in different places.
Shows the world's average air and sea surface temperature each day, compared with historical averages. This dataset is often used to track record heat and communicate how fast the climate is warming.

Shows how much greenhouse gas each country emits by sector, including emissions from land use change and forestry. This dataset is often used to compare countries and track progress against climate commitments (NDCs).

Shows each country's carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels and from land use change, along with how much carbon oceans and land absorb. This dataset is often used as the scientific reference for the global carbon balance.

Shows estimated greenhouse gas emissions from individual sources such as power plants, farms, and forest clearing, using satellites and AI. This dataset is often used to see where emissions come from within a country, not just national totals.

Shows how much of the available water in each river basin is already being used. Higher values mean more competition for water and greater risk of shortages. This layer is often used to assess water risk for agriculture, cities, and investments, now and in the future.

Shows what covers every 10 m patch of land worldwide, sorted into 11 classes such as tree cover, cropland, grassland, built-up areas, and wetlands. This layer is often used as a detailed baseline for land use planning and ecosystem mapping.

Shows land cover worldwide each year, including the percentage of each pixel covered by trees, shrubs, grass, crops, and other surfaces. This layer is often used where mixed landscapes matter, such as savannas and farm mosaics.

Shows near real-time land cover for every satellite pass, with the likelihood of each of nine classes such as water, trees, crops, and built-up area. This layer is often used to see recent and seasonal changes, such as flooding or crop cycles.
Shows global land cover every year since 2001 under several classification systems. Its long, consistent record makes it a standard input for land change studies and earth system models.

Shows how often each location has been covered by water since 1984. Higher values mean permanent water; lower values mean seasonal or occasional flooding. This layer is often used to track shrinking lakes, new reservoirs, and wetland change.

Shows where trees have been removed or died each year since 2001, whether from clearing, fire, or disease. This layer is often used to monitor deforestation and to support forest policy and supply chain commitments.
Source: World Resources Institute (WRI) and University of Maryland
More Information: Global Forest Watch Open Data Portal

Description: Shows official country figures on how much forest each country has, how it is changing, and how much carbon it stores. This dataset is often used for national reporting and international comparisons of forest trends.
Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN (FAO)

Description: Shows where tropical rainforests have been cleared, degraded, or are regrowing each year since 1990. Unlike most forest maps, it separates degradation from full deforestation. This layer is often used for REDD+ and deforestation-free trade monitoring.

Shows where mangrove forests grow along the world's coasts and how their extent has changed since 1996. This layer is often used for coastal protection planning, blue carbon projects, and restoration targeting.
Source: Global Mangrove Alliance partners (Aberystwyth University, JAXA, and others)

Description: Shows each country's reported trends in land cover, land productivity, and soil organic carbon, the three measures of land degradation under SDG 15.3.1. This dataset is often used to track progress toward land degradation neutrality targets.

Shows the boundaries of national parks, reserves, and other protected and conserved areas worldwide. This layer is often used to measure progress toward conservation targets such as 30x30 and to screen projects for environmental risk.

Shows how much of each area is covered by buildings and how settlements have grown since 1975, with projections to 2030. This layer is often used to track urban sprawl onto farmland and natural areas.

Shows how many people live in each small grid cell across every country. Higher values mean more densely populated areas. This layer is often used to estimate how many people depend on or are affected by a landscape, hazard, or project.

Shows lands held or used by Indigenous Peoples and local communities, including whether their rights are formally recognized. This layer is often used to respect land rights in conservation and development planning.
Source: LandMark partners (WRI, Rights and Resources Initiative, and others)

Description: Shows living standards, health, and education for more than 1,700 regions within countries. Higher values mean better human development outcomes. This dataset is often used to spot regional inequality hidden in national averages.

Shows each country's overall level of human development based on life expectancy, education, and income, with related gender and poverty indices. This dataset is often used for cross-country comparisons of wellbeing.
Shows how women and men compare on education, work, health, and ownership of land and assets. This dataset is often used to understand gender gaps in access to land and natural resources.

Shows how severe hunger is in each area, on a five-phase scale from minimal to famine, and how many people are affected. Higher phases mean more urgent need. This dataset is often used to prioritize humanitarian response.
Source: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification partnership (FAO, WFP, and others)

Description: Shows each country's risk of humanitarian crisis based on hazard exposure, vulnerability, and capacity to cope. Higher scores mean greater risk. This dataset is often used to prioritize disaster preparedness and resilience investment.
Source: Joint Research Centre, European Commission, and UN OCHA
More Information: JRC / Disaster Risk Management Knowledge Centre

Description: Shows how many people have been forced to leave their homes within their own country because of conflict or disasters such as floods and droughts. This dataset is often used to understand the human impacts of climate and land-related shocks.

Dataset Name: ESA CCI Global Forest Above Ground Biomass
Description: Estimates forest above-ground biomass using SAR and Earth observation data.

Shows the number of refugees, asylum-seekers, and other displaced people by where they come from and where they are hosted. This dataset is often used to plan support for host communities and displaced populations.

Shows how long it takes to reach the nearest healthcare facility from any location worldwide. Higher values mean more remote, underserved areas. This layer is often used to identify communities cut off from essential services.
Source: Malaria Atlas Project (University of Oxford / Telethon Kids Institute)

Dataset Name: Crop Suitability and Potential Yield (GAEZ v4)
Description: Shows how suitable land is for growing specific crops and how much it could produce under current and future climates. Higher values mean better growing conditions. This layer is often used to plan agricultural investment and adaptation.

Dataset Name: Land Cover and Land Use Statistics (FAOSTAT)
Description: Shows how much land in each country is cropland, pasture, forest, and other uses, and how that has changed over decades. This dataset is often used to track agricultural expansion and compare land use across countries.
Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN (FAO)
Timeframe: Land cover 1992–recent year; land use 1961–recent year

Description: Shows the share of each country's land covered by forest over time. This indicator is often used in development reporting and to compare forest trends alongside economic data.

Shows large land deals for agriculture, forestry, and mining, including who is investing, where, and how much land is involved. This dataset is often used to monitor land grabbing and investment pressure on local communities.
Source: Land Matrix Initiative (ILC, CIRAD, GIGA, CDE, and others)

Description: Shows where more than 40 crops are grown and how much each area produces. Higher values mean more intensive production. This layer is often used to link land use to food supply and agricultural value.

Shows how much organic carbon is stored in the top 30cm of soil worldwide — the layer most affected by farming, grazing, and land use. Higher values generally mean healthier, more fertile soil. This layer is often used to track soil health and carbon loss from agriculture.

Shows the boundaries of officially recognised protected areas across the world's land and oceans — national parks, marine reserves, wildlife sanctuaries, and similar. Useful for checking whether a project site, region, or piece of land overlaps with a protected area. Updated monthly with submissions from governments and conservation organisations.

Shows the location of roughly 30,000 power plants worldwide, along with the fuel type each one uses (coal, gas, hydro, solar, wind, nuclear, etc.) and how much electricity it can generate. Useful for looking at where power generation — and its associated emissions or resource use — happens across a country or region.

This dataset shows forecasted and historical streamflow (water discharge) for over 7 million river and stream reaches worldwide, updated daily using weather data from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). Useful for spotting potential flooding, monitoring water availability, and tracking river conditions in near real time — including in places with no ground-based river gauges.
Timeframe: Forecast: rolling 10-day, updated daily (3-hour intervals) · Historical simulation: 1940–present, updated weekly
